findings.finding: longValue() overflow assumption is now documented with a comment at renderValue() line 153-154 (YAGNI + CustomFieldValueValidator guarantee). Addressed.
Objects.requireNonNull(subscriber, "subscriber") added at the top of render() (line 63-64). Addressed.
loneClosingBraceWithoutOpenerIsLiteral() test added. Bonus test closingBracesAfterPlaceholderLeaveLoneBrace() also added to cover the '}}' after a placeholder case. Addressed.

HTML double-quote escaping: case '"' -> sb.append(""") added to escapeHtml(). Logic is correct — Telegram HTML mode decodes " as a standard named entity, so legitimate quotes display correctly while attribute-injection via a raw " is now blocked. The None/HTML/MarkdownV2 branch ordering in escape() is unchanged.

MarkdownV2 backslash escaping: condition widened to (c == '\\' || MARKDOWN_V2_SPECIALS.indexOf(c) >= 0). The implementation iterates the original value char-by-char in a single pass, so an emitted '\\' is never re-processed. Input '\\*' produces '\\\\\\*' (Java source) which is the string '\\\*' — correct Telegram encoding for a literal backslash followed by a literal '*'. The dedicated regression test markdownV2EscapesBackslashToPreventInjection() and the updated markdownV2ModeEscapesFullCharset() test both encode the expected values correctly. Author markup in the template (e.g. *bold*) is still emitted via out.append(c) in the main render loop and never passes through escape(), confirming it remains untouched.

summary: All three round-1 minors are resolved: the longValue() assumption is documented, subscriber is null-checked with requireNonNull, and the lone-'}' edge case has a test. The new escape-logic changes (HTML '"' → ", MarkdownV2 backslash self-escape) are correct and clean: single-pass char iteration prevents double-processing, None/HTML/MarkdownV2 ordering is unchanged, and author markup in templates remains untouched. Two new regression tests (htmlModeEscapesDoubleQuoteInAttribute, markdownV2EscapesBackslashToPreventInjection) directly pin the fixed vulnerabilities. No new findings.
